subject: CAIQ response consolidation and DocuSign orchestration
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@palisadebank.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ + next steps for procurement + signature

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Procurement and InfoSec are ready to move forward but need a consolidated CAIQ package and a control-to-evidence mapping we can hand to our audit team. Specific asks:

- Completed CAIQ spreadsheet (cells with short narratives where necessary)
- Control ownership grid indicating internal SMEs and artifact filenames
- Two representative evidence samples (telemetry/log sample and key-rotation proof)
- A DocuSign route for the attestation page once we confirm items

Can you confirm cadence to deliver the draft and whether Redwood can provide a short transmittal note that explains any non-standard responses (exceptions/compensating controls)? We’d like to line up a brief call the week of Sep 6 to walk the package with our auditors.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Sr. Procurement Manager
Palisade Bank

(Attachments requested: CAIQ template, evidence checklist)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@palisadebank.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ + next steps for procurement + signature

Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks. We’ll assemble a consolidated package and propose a handoff timeline:

1) By Wed 2027-09-01 EOD: draft CAIQ workbook with control-level notes and owner column (attached: Redwood_CAIQ_Response_v0.9.xlsx)
2) By Thu 2027-09-02: control ownership CSV and two sample artifacts uploaded to the shared Drive
3) By Fri 2027-09-03: DocuSign link for the attestation page (once you confirm signatories)

Jordan, Kimberly — can you own the CAIQ narrative sweep and the log retention sample respectively? I’ve started a control ownership grid (control-ownership-grid.csv) and will drop it in the Drive.

Elena — I’ll include a short transmittal note that flags any answers where we call out compensating controls (we try to keep exceptions minimal). If procurement needs a redlines-friendly statement for legal, we can provide that too.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_CAIQ_Response_v0.9.xlsx (draft)
From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ + next steps for procurement + signature

Marissa / Kimberly —

I’ll take the CAIQ narrative sweep (A.1-A.6 + data residency questions). I’ll check the sections that typically require a short architecture note (network segregation, tenant isolation, key management).

Kimberly — could you confirm which runtime logs we can share as a sanitized sample? I want to ensure we don’t include any tenant identifiers. If you point me to the sanitized extract we typically use, I’ll annotate the narrative to reference the exact file.

FYI: I’ll also flag two controls where we’ve historically recommended a compensating control (token-level redaction / per-tenant telemetry guardrails).

Thanks —J

Hi all,

I uploaded two sanitized samples to the shared Drive folder: log-retention-sample.txt and key-rotation-proof.pdf (redacted). The log file is scrubbed of tenant IDs and IPs; it contains trace-level events that align to controls CCM-3 and CCM-7.

Also attached here is control-ownership-grid.csv with owner emails and a short note on evidence locations. I set retention language in the narrative to reflect our standard 365-day retention for runtime telemetry and a 7-year retention for key custody metadata. If Palisade needs alternate retention language, legal will need to sign off — happy to loop them if necessary.

Kimberly Park
Director, Production Security
Redwood Inference
